predecessors.name: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom
predecessors.text: Transylvania and the Partium, which John II Sigismund Zapolya held as King of Hungary until the Treaty of Speyer (infobox: Predecessor 'Eastern Hungarian Kingdom')

successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: Transylvania, 'formally attached to Habsburg-controlled Hungary, and subjected to the direct rule of the emperor's governors' after the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz

ledger.x: 1570: John II Sigismund Zapolya becomes prince of Transylvania under the Treaty of Speyer.
October 1599: Michael the Brave of Wallachia takes Transylvania as imperial governor.
September 1600: Michael is driven out of Transylvania.
1600: the Habsburgs rule through General Basta.
21 February 1605: Stephen Bocskai is elected Prince of Transylvania at Nyárádszereda, ending Habsburg rule.
August 1619: Gabriel Bethlen invades Habsburg Royal Hungary.
31 December 1621: the Peace of Nikolsburg ends the war between Bethlen and Ferdinand II ('signed on 31 December 1621 in Nikolsburg').
31 December 1621: Bethlen receives seven counties in northern Hungary at Nikolsburg.
27 August 1660: Nagyvárad falls to the Ottomans and becomes the seat of a pasha.
19 November 1682: Thokoly's Principality of Upper Hungary appears over 23,014 km2 that Cliopatria has been drawing in Transylvania.
15 October 1685: Thokoly's principality ends and the north-western counties are drawn in Transylvania again.
1691: a 1,106 km2 trim on the south-west edge, five of whose cells are in Cliopatria's Ottoman 1691 shape.
1692: the capital moves from Gyulafehervar (Alba Iulia) to Cibinium (Sibiu).
26 January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz passes Transylvania to the Habsburgs.

wars.name: Gabriel Bethlen's war in Royal Hungary
wars.outcome: Bethlen won seven counties around the Upper Tisza, the fortresses of Tokaj, Munkács and Ecsed, a Silesian duchy and the title of imperial prince at the Peace of Nikolsburg, 31 December 1621; the emperor 'reconquer[ed] most of Royal Hungary by 1621'.

wars.name: Michael the Brave's conquest of Transylvania (Battle of Șelimbăr)
wars.outcome: Michael beat Cardinal Andrew Bathory at Selimbar on 18 October 1599 and ruled as imperial governor to September 1600, when Hungarian nobles and Basta beat him at Miraslau; he was killed on 9 August 1601.

wars.name: Bocskai uprising
wars.outcome: Bocskai's successful rebellion (28 September 1604-23 June 1606) ended with the Treaty of Vienna, recognizing him as sovereign prince of an 'enlarged Principality of Transylvania' with religious liberty and the right to elect princes.

wars.name: Ottoman and Tatar wars on Transylvania (George II Rakoczi's Polish campaign and its aftermath)
wars.outcome: 'In 1657, George II Rákóczi invaded the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth'; wars then ravaged the principality from 1657 to 1661 ('the Partium and the counties of Belső-Szolnok, Doboka, Kolozs, Közép-Szolnok, and Kraszna were laid waste'); Nagyvárad fell to the…

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Habsburgs won; the Treaty of Karlowitz (26 January 1699) 'secured territories, the rest of Hungary and overlordship of Transylvania for the Austrians'.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey: the frontiers with the Habsburg kingdom, Moldavia, Wallachia and the Ottoman Banat follow counties and mountains approximately.
The north-eastern frontier is fixed by county at Nikolsburg (31 December 1621); the Ottoman and Danubian-principality frontiers stay approximate.
The Ottoman Varat Eyalet and Habsburg fronts move with the Great Turkish War; Karlowitz (1699) is a treaty but the page names no boundary.
